evals.prompt: I have 340 AI-search prompts for TrailForge, a fictional hiking-boot brand on example.com, in prompts.csv with Search Console impressions. Cluster them into pages and tell me which existing page each prompt belongs on and where we need new pages.
evals.expected_output: A prompt-to-page map built from Google SERP overlap: a prompt master with hash ids, a SERP fetched for every prompt before clustering, centroid-greedy clusters on the top 10 with T=2 and the df-guarded 1-shared rule, rank-weighted page assignment with row-level evidence, a short list of demand-verified new pages, the five gates run, and the citations-proxy caveat stated.
expectations: Builds a prompt master with stable ids (md5 of normalized text) and states fetched-SERP count equals prompt count before clustering
Stores top-20 results but clusters on the top 10, and uses ranks 11-20 only for near-miss refresh flags
Applies T=2 shared URLs, and joins on one shared URL only when its document frequency is 5 or less, it is not a hub host and the prompt is not a brand comparison
Sends every 1-shared join to a topicality hand-read instead of auto-accepting it
Assigns pages with brand-URL consensus where 2+ member SERPs at best rank 5 or better gives high confidence and worse ranks are rank-demoted to medium
Treats unplaced singletons as a negative test and checks seed demand, trend, seed ownership at full depth and the real page inventory before proposing any new page
Runs the integrity, grain, reconciliation and fidelity scripts and reports their exact output lines
States that Google organic overlap is a proxy for answer-engine citations

evals.prompt: We're launching a new site for Harborline Kayak Tours (fictional, harborline.example) so none of the pages exist yet. I have 28 planned page URLs, each with 3-6 verified keywords, and 150 prompts. Place the prompts on the planned pages.
evals.expected_output: Recognises that brand-URL consensus cannot fire on an all-create page set, builds each page's profile from SERPs for up to 5 of its keywords, scores clusters by rank-weighted shared URLs discounted by inverse page frequency, requires a 25% margin and marks near-ties AMBIGUOUS with both candidates, reports pairwise profile overlap as merge questions, and records a placement basis on every prompt.
expectations: Explains that signal A cannot fire because the brand ranks for nothing yet, and switches to keyword-built page profiles
Fetches SERPs for up to 5 keywords per page and unions their non-hub top 10 into the page profile
Weights each shared URL by inverse page frequency across the page set, not only corpus document frequency
Marks a cluster AMBIGUOUS and names both candidate pages with scores when the runner-up is within 25% of the winner
Reports pairwise page-profile overlap and treats near-identical profiles as a merge question, letting head-term separation win when deep and head-term overlap disagree
Labels every prompt with one of the placement bases (SERP, HAND, JOB-OVERRIDE, FRAME, COMPRESSION, SECTION, NEW-PAGE) and counts them on the methodology tab
Proposes one hub rather than many thin pages when the new-page set is small cuts of one subject

evals.prompt: The page map for Copperleaf Garden Tools (fictional, example.org) came back from the client with comments in a column. Most pages only have one or two keywords. Action the comments, top up the thin pages with more keywords and give each page a priority score.
evals.expected_output: Agrees the comment legend first and reads comments as BUILD / FOLD / DROP / MOVE / approved-but-unplaced, never edits the reviewer column, treats un-commented rows as not reviewed, applies folds on the keyword sheet and reports score movement; backfills 2-10 keywords per thin page from the keywords already-ranking URLs rank for, using seed-containment, distinct-facet and not-elsewhere tests with a written reason per row; computes the KOB-based Opportunity Score by percentile rank without scoring missing CPC as zero; and re-runs the remap and reconciliation checks.
expectations: Agrees the comment legend with the user before interpreting comments, and reads a rejection that offers a merge as a FOLD
Leaves the reviewer's column untouched and marks un-commented rows as not reviewed rather than approved
Applies folds on the keyword sheet, zeroes the absorbed page's rollups and names what the survivor page must now carry
Sources backfill keywords from what the URLs already ranking in each page's SERP rank for, not from a generic idea tool or slug fragments
Keeps 2 to 10 keywords per page, allows zero, and applies seed containment, distinct facet and a whole-sheet duplicate check with a reason per kept row
Checks what the owner of each source URL sells and rejects off-subject high-volume candidates
Scores pages with KOB 60 / Volume 25 / Trend 15 by percentile rank, impressions as an uplift, redistributes weight when CPC is missing, and labels keyword-less pages in words
Re-runs the post-review remap check and the reconciliation gate after backfill

evals.prompt: Quick sanity check before I send this prompt-to-page workbook for NorthPeak Climbing Gyms (fictional): the integrity gate passed. Anything else I need to verify?
evals.expected_output: Points out that a passing final gate is not proof the pipeline ran, and lists the remaining checks: exit codes on every step, grain check, reconciliation gate, fidelity re-fetch, 1-shared and low-confidence hand-reads, URL status gate on refresh/create rows, placement basis counts, drift quarantine on category vocabulary, content mix re-run, row-level evidence columns populated, zero formula errors and the citations caveat.
expectations: Warns that a crashed earlier step can leave stale artifacts that later gates pass on, so every step's exit code must be checked
Requires the URL status gate: 200 with no redirect stays REFRESH, a redirect to another page flips to CREATE, and 404s are confirmed too
Requires 1-shared joins and authored-intent rows to have been hand-read
Checks that carried columns such as intent are populated, not just present
Checks final row count equals the prompt-master count and the workbook has zero formula errors
Confirms the deliverable states the Google-organic-as-citation-proxy caveat
